string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of China and an important centre for government, culture and international exchange. It lies at the northern edge of the North China Plain, with mountains to the west and north. The city has a history of more than three thousand years and served as the capital during several dynasties, including the Yuan, Ming and Qing. Historic places such as the Forbidden City show its long role in Chinese history. The municipality also includes sections of the Great Wall. Beijing has hot, rainy summers and cold, dry winters, with shorter spring and autumn seasons.

Shanghai is a municipality on the eastern coast of China, near the mouth of the Yangtze River. Its position connects the Yangtze River Delta with sea routes and supports its role in trade and shipping. Shanghai County was established in 1292, and the city later developed into a major trading port. Today, Shanghai is also an important financial and economic centre. The Huangpu River separates Puxi from Pudong. Historic buildings along the Bund face the modern skyline across the water. The development of Pudong, launched in 1990, brought major changes to the city and its international business activities.

Chongqing is a municipality in southwestern China on the upper reaches of the Yangtze River. Its central urban area lies where the Yangtze and Jialing rivers meet. Mountains, hills and river valleys shape the city, which is often called the Mountain City. Chongqing became a municipality directly under the central government in 1997. Its territory includes a large urban centre as well as smaller towns, farmland and mountainous areas. The rivers support transport and connect different parts of the region. Jiefangbei is a well known landmark and a busy commercial area with shops, restaurants, hotels and other businesses.

Tianjin is a municipality in northern China beside the Bohai Sea and close to Beijing. The Haihe River passes through the city and has long supported transport and trade. Tianjin was established as a military garrison in 1404 during the Ming Dynasty. It later became an important port, and buildings from different periods still reflect its history. Today, Tianjin serves as a major maritime gateway for northern China. Binhai New Area contains the port and important industrial areas. The city combines riverfront streets and historic architecture with modern manufacturing, shipping and transport links to the wider region.
